steps.title: At the foot of Aconcagua
steps.body: Mendoza lies in western Argentina, at the foot of the Andes, near Aconcagua, the highest mountain outside Asia, at 6,961 m. It makes about 70% of Argentina's wine, with around 150,000 hectares of vines. Vineyards range from about 600 to 1,600 m in altitude.

steps.title: High desert
steps.body: Mendoza is a high desert, with about 200 to 250 mm of rain a year, in the Andes' rain shadow. Summers are hot and sunny, nights cool, with a large day and night swing. Low humidity means little disease. Hail is the biggest threat; many vineyards use hail nets. The Zonda, a hot, dry wind, can damage vines in spring.

steps.prompt: What is the biggest weather threat in Mendoza?
steps.explanation: Summer hailstorms can destroy crops; nets protect vines.

steps.title: Irrigation
steps.body: Without irrigation, Mendoza couldn't grow vines. Snowmelt from the Andes feeds rivers like the Mendoza and Tunuyán. The Huarpe people built channels before the Spanish arrived; the Spanish expanded them. Today, flood, furrow and drip irrigation all draw on this water. Water rights are precious, and drought years are a growing concern.

steps.prompt: Mendoza's vineyards depend on irrigation from Andean snowmelt.
steps.explanation: Yes. It's a desert without it.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Mendoza makes about 70% of Argentina's wine, under the Andes
It's a high, dry desert; hail is the main threat
Snowmelt irrigation, via ancient channels, makes it possible
